title: Disc-jet coupling changes as a possible indicator for outbursts from GX 339-4 remaining within the X-ray hard state
question: Can X-ray or radio/(sub-)mm disk-jet coupling signatures act as indicators for whether an outburst of GX 339-4 will remain in the hard X-ray spectral state ('hard-only') rather than completing a full outburst?

what.value: Radio and X-ray luminosities for the 2008, 2009, and 2012 hard-only outbursts and five successful outbursts of GX 339-4

evidence.quote: To extend the X-ray luminosity range, we combined our 2017–2018 $L_{\rm r} - L_{\rm X}$ data with radio and X-ray luminosities taken from other hard-only outbursts from GX 339$-$4 (Figure 9, left panel), where we include data presented by (cite: corbel) on the 2008, 2009 and 2012 hard-only outbursts.

what.value: Interstellar abundances and photoionization cross-sections for X-ray spectral fitting, and fixed hydrogen column density value for comparison

evidence.quote: The tbabs model component, making use of abundances from (cite: 2000ApJ...542..914W), and photoionization cross-sections from (cite: 1996ApJ...465..487V), was used to account for interstellar absorption.

We also compared all results with $N_{\rm H}$ either fixed to literature values ($N_{\rm H}$$_{\rm ,fixed} = 0.851 \times 10^{22}$ cm$^{-2}$; (cite: 2015ApJ...808..122F)), or left free (untied) for all epochs

recipe.goal: Reduce and image ALMA sub-mm continuum and measure integrated and sub-band flux densities
recipe.method: Multi-frequency synthesis continuum imaging in CASA using tclean with natural weighting (both full 8 GHz bands and 2 GHz sub-bands), followed by point source fitting in the image plane with imfit
key_parameters: natural weighting; central frequencies 97.5, 145, 233 GHz (8 GHz full bandwidth and 2 GHz sub-bands)
assumptions: 5% systematic uncertainty on absolute flux density calibration for ALMA bands <350 GHz

recipe.goal: Reduce and image ATCA radio continuum and measure flux densities, luminosities, and spectral indices
recipe.method: Standard calibration and natural-weighted imaging in CASA, image-plane Gaussian fitting with FWHM fixed to the synthesised beam, and Monte Carlo fitting for spectral index alpha
assumptions: Source distance D = 8 kpc; systematic flux scale uncertainty of 2% at 5.5/9 GHz and 4% at 17/19 GHz

recipe.goal: Extract intra-observational radio and sub-mm light curves and quantify short-timescale variability
recipe.method: Extract 5-min time-resolved ATCA light curves at 5.5 and 9 GHz using UVMULTIFIT in the uv-plane and 30-sec time-resolved ALMA sub-mm light curves across Bands 3, 4, and 6, then compute fractional RMS variability statistic F_var
key_parameters: 5-min time intervals for ATCA; 30-sec time intervals for ALMA
assumptions: Point source (delta function in uv-plane for ATCA)

recipe.goal: Fit X-ray spectra and measure X-ray fluxes, photon indices, hardness ratios, and luminosities
recipe.method: Fit 0.5-10 keV Swift-XRT spectra in XSPEC with an absorbed power-law (tbabs*powerlaw) and extract unabsorbed fluxes with cflux; convert MAXI 2-20 keV count rates during Sun constraint to 1-10 keV fluxes using WebPIMMS
key_parameters: Energy bands: 1–10 keV, 0.5–10 keV, 0.5–1.5 keV, and 1.5–10 keV; tied N_H = (0.56 +/- 0.02) x 10^22 cm^-2
assumptions: Distance D = 8 kpc; M_BH = 7.8 M_sun for Eddington luminosity; Gamma = 1.5 - 2.5 for MAXI flux conversion

recipe.goal: Fit the radio-X-ray luminosity correlation and compare hard-only vs successful outbursts
recipe.method: Perform linear regression in logarithmic space on quasi-simultaneous radio and X-ray luminosities using Python LINMIX_ERR (10,000 iterations), and compare hard-only and successful outburst distributions with a Monte-Carlo 2D 2-sample K-S test
key_parameters: 10,000 iterations in LINMIX_ERR; quasi-simultaneous data within 1 day (MJD 58058 interpolated assuming exponential rise)
assumptions: Power-law relation between L_r and L_X (linear in logarithmic space)

evidence.quote: However, quasi-simultaneous radio and X-ray observations showed a flatter than expected coupling between the radio and X-ray luminosities (with a best fit relation of $L_{\rm radio} \propto L_{\rm X}^{0.39 \pm 0.06}$), when compared to successful outbursts from this system ($L_{\rm radio} \propto L_{\rm X}^{0.62 \pm 0.02}$).
finding a flatter than usual radio – X-ray coupling for GX 339$-$4, where $L_{\rm r} \propto L_{\rm X}^{0.39 \pm 0.06}$ for this hard-only outburst (Figure 8).

answer_key.quantity: Radio-X-ray luminosity correlation slope for 2017-2018 hard-only outburst (excluding MAXI)

evidence.quote: As such, excluding the MAXI points did not change our results, providing a best-fit relation of $L_{\rm r} \propto L_{\rm X}^{0.3 \pm 0.1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Radio-X-ray luminosity correlation slope for combined hard-only outbursts of GX 339-4

evidence.quote: including data from other hard-only outbursts from GX 339$-$4 extends the luminosity range to $\sim$1.2 and $\sim$2.8 orders of magnitude, respectively, and also results in a flatter correlation (where $L_{\rm radio} \propto L_{\rm X}^{0.46 \pm 0.04}$).

We find a best-fit relation of $L_{\rm r} \propto L_{\rm X}^{0.46 \pm 0.04}$ ($L_{\rm r} \propto L_{\rm X}^{0.44 \pm 0.07}$ without the MAXI data), again much flatter than the $L_{\rm r} \propto L_{\rm X}^{0.62 \pm 0.02}$ relation for the successful outbursts from GX 339$-$4

answer_key.quantity: Radio-X-ray luminosity correlation slope for successful outbursts of GX 339-4

evidence.quote: We find a best-fit relation of $L_{\rm r} \propto L_{\rm X}^{0.46 \pm 0.04}$ ($L_{\rm r} \propto L_{\rm X}^{0.44 \pm 0.07}$ without the MAXI data), again much flatter than the $L_{\rm r} \propto L_{\rm X}^{0.62 \pm 0.02}$ relation for the successful outbursts from GX 339$-$4

answer_key.quantity: 2D 2-sample K-S test p-value comparing hard-only and successful L_r-L_X distributions

evidence.quote: Performing a Monte-Carlo 2-dimensional 2-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) test (cite: 1983MNRAS.202..615P; 1987MNRAS.225..155F) on the successful and hard-only data sets yields a $p$-value of 0.031
